I want to talk about the second sentence, because that is where most people lose the conversation. Somebody asks you how the weekend was, and you say it was good. That answer is correct, it is polite, and it closes the door. The other person has nothing to hold on to, so they change the subject, and two minutes later you are both looking at your phones. The fix is not more vocabulary. The fix is one more sentence, and the easiest one is a reason. It was good, because we finally got out of the city. It was good, so we are going back in November. Notice what happens to the other person. Now they know about the city and about November, and they have two doors to walk through. You did not become fluent. You added six words.

If you are going to South Florida at the end of October, here is what the numbers say. The water is still warm, around twenty-seven degrees, and the afternoons are hot, but the heavy rain of the summer is finished, so most days are dry. It is also the start of the busy season, which means the beach is crowded from Friday to Sunday and much quieter on a Tuesday morning. You do not need a car. The buses along the beach run every fifteen minutes, and the trolley is free, so a lot of visitors end up walking more than they expected. One last thing that surprises people. The last bus back from the neighbourhoods south of the river is earlier than you think, so check the time before you sit down for dinner.
